dashboard.label: Lab Info
dashboard.description: What this lab is, how it is built, and where the code lives.

html.p: A self-rebuilding Splunk lab for Cisco dCloud. The environment resets to an empty template each session, so on every startup a script pulls this project from GitHub and re-creates the full configuration from scratch: per-location indexes, RBAC roles, users, and dashboards. Nothing here is configured by hand - it is all code, so the lab is identical every time.
html.h3: What gets pre-loaded on each session

ul.li: 6 indexes, one namespace per location: loc1_*, loc2_*, loc3_*
3 RBAC roles: role_loc1 (loc1 only), role_loc2 (loc2 only), role_global (all)
Dashboards: Lab Info (this page), Setup Status, Ingestion & Health

html.p: Start here, then open Setup Status to confirm everything loaded correctly before the demo begins.

search.query: | rest /services/server/info | eval uptime_hours=round(startup_time_delta/3600,1) | rename version as Version, build as Build, os_name as OS, cpu_arch as Arch, numberOfCores as Cores, serverName as Host, uptime_hours as "Uptime (h)" | table Version Build OS Arch Cores Host "Uptime (h)"

html.p: On each session start, dCloud Startup Automation runs one command that fixes DNS, clones this repo, and applies the config:
To change the lab, edit the repo and push to main - the next session picks it up automatically.
